units.intro: Grammar: the past tenses (simple, continuous, perfect) and how they work together in sentences with when, while, before and after.

cards.title: Past tenses (review)
rule: **Past simple** (verb + -ed or irregular form) = a finished action at a past time: *She **won** the race in 2019.*
**Past continuous** (was/were + -ing) = an action in progress at a past moment: *At 8 pm they **were studying**.*
**Past perfect** (had + past participle) = an action that happened **before** another past action: *The film **had started** when we arrived.*

examples.text: I visited my aunt last week.
I was visit my aunt last week.
examples.fix: I visited my aunt last week.

examples.text: When I arrived, the meeting had already begun.
She has finished the work yesterday.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The scholarship committee awarded the funding to Aster and ________ after reviewing our academic portfolios.

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The pronoun follows the preposition 'to' and forms part of a compound prepositional object ('to Aster and [pronoun]').
This slot requires the objective case ($$\text{Preposition} + \text{Object Pronoun}$$).
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often write 'Aster and I' because 'Aster and I' is common in the subject position.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The old typewriter in the headmaster's office is still functional, but ________ keys are difficult to press.

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The blank modifies the noun 'keys' to show ownership.
This requires the possessive adjective 'its'.
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often confuse 'its' (possessive adjective) with 'it's' (contraction of 'it is' or 'it has').

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The candidate ________ the board selected for the position has outstanding credentials.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The relative pronoun refers to 'The candidate' (a person). The clause that follows has a subject-verb pattern: 'the board' (Subject) + 'selected' (Verb). This indicates the relative pronoun is acting as the object of 'selected'.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
While 'who' is increasingly used as an object pronoun in casual speech, formal academic exams strictly enforce 'whom' for objective relative slots ($$\text{Whom} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$).

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ ተውላጠ ስም ን 'The candidate' (ሰብ) ክውክል ከሎ፡ ድሕሪኡ ዘሎ ሓረግ 'the board selected' (Subject + Verb) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ እቲ ተውላጠ ስም ኣብ ቦታ ተቐባሊ (object) እዩ ዘሎ። ስለዚ ኣብ ስሩዕ ሰዋስው 'whom' (Option B) ክንጥቀም ኣለና። 'Who' ኣብ ናይ ዋና ባእታ (subject) ቦታ ጥራይ እዩ ዝስራዕ።

cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The subject is 'they' (plural). The corresponding plural reflexive pronoun is 'themselves' ($$\text{They} \rightarrow \text{themselves}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Options A ('theirselves') and D ('by theirselves') are non-standard forms. Tigrinya speakers often use 'theirselves' because they translate 'ባዕላቶም' directly based on the possessive modifier 'their'.

cards.title: Past tenses in adverbial clauses
rule: **Past continuous + past simple:** a longer action interrupted by a short one: *While she **was cooking**, the phone **rang**.*
**Past perfect + past simple:** the earlier action uses the past perfect: *After he **had finished** his homework, he **went** out.*
Use **while** with the longer (continuous) action and **when** usually with the short action.

examples.text: While we were walking home, it started to rain.
While we walked home, it was starting to rain.
examples.fix: While we were walking home, it started to rain.

examples.text: Before the teacher came, we had cleaned the class.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "While we walked home, it was starting to rain."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** **Past continuous + past simple:** a longer action interrupted by a short one: *While she **was cooking**, the phone **rang**.*
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "While we walked home, it was starting to rain." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "While we were walking home, it started to rain."
**Check:** **Past perfect + past simple:** the earlier action uses the past perfect: *After he **had finished** his homework, he **went** out.*

cards.answer: While we were walking home, it started to rain.

units.title: The Internet and You
units.intro: Grammar: active and passive voice in the present, past and future simple, and when to use the passive.

cards.title: Active and passive (1)
rule: In the **active** the subject does the action: *People **use** the Internet.* In the **passive** the subject receives the action: *The Internet **is used** by people.*
**Form:** be (in the right tense) + past participle. Present: is/are + pp; past: was/were + pp; future: will be + pp.
The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive; the doer can be added with **by**.

examples.text: Emails are sent every second.
The message was send yesterday.
The new café will be opened next week.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The manager rejected the proposal because he felt that ________ details were provided to support the budget.

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The blank modifies the noun 'details'. 'Details' is a plural countable noun (indicated by the '-s' ending).
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Uncountable quantifiers like 'little' and 'a little' cannot modify plural countable nouns. 'Too few' is the correct quantifier for countable nouns in a negative context.
Tigrinya speakers often conflate 'few' and 'little' as both translate to 'ውሑድ' or 'ቅሩብ'.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Although the construction project has been delayed, ________ progress has been made this week.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Progress' is an uncountable noun in English. It cannot be pluralized and cannot pair with countable quantifiers.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
'A few' and 'many' are strictly countable. 'Few' is also countable. 'Some' can modify both countable and uncountable nouns, making it the only grammatically viable option here.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Progress' (ዕብየት/ምስጓም) ዘይቝጸር ስም (uncountable noun) እዩ። 'Many' ን 'a few' ን ንዝቝጸሩ ስማት ጥራይ ስለ ዝኾኑ ምስ 'progress' ክኸዱ ኣይኽእሉን። 'Some' ግን ምስ ክልቲኦም ስለ ዝኸይድ ቅኑዕ መልሲ Option C እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The police ________ investigating the robbery that occurred near the national bank.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Police' is a collective noun that is grammatically plural and always takes a plural verb.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Because 'police' does not end in '-s', many non-native speakers mistake it for a singular noun and pair it with singular verbs like 'is' or 'was'. This is a highly targeted agreement trap in the ESSLCE.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Police' (ፖሊስ) ዝብል ስም ክትርእዮ ከለኻ ናይ ነጸላ (singular) ይመስል እምበር፡ ብሰዋስው ግን ወትሩ ብዙሕ ቁጽሪ (plural) ተገይሩ ስለ ዝውሰድ ድሕሪኡ ዝመጽእ ግሲ 'are' (Option B) ክኸውን ኣለዎ።

cards.q: You must clean this machine every time you use it. (Choose the correct passive form)

options.A: This machine must clean every time.
options.B: This machine must be cleaned every time.
options.C: Every time must clean this machine.
options.D: This machine must be cleaned every time it is used.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** Identify the structure. "must clean" is a modal active.
**Step 2:** The passive of a modal is **modal + be + Past Participle**. 
**Step 3:** "This machine must be cleaned..." matches. Choice D is more complete because it also converts "you use it" to "it is used".

cards.title: Uses of the passive
rule: Use the passive when the **doer is unknown** (*My phone was stolen.*), when the **receiver is more important** (*The results will be announced on Monday.*), or when the doer is **obvious** (*He was arrested.* — by the police).
Leave out *by + doer* when it adds nothing (*by someone, by people*).

cards.title: Parts of speech (1)

cards.title: Linking words
rule: **and** adds, **but** contrasts, **or** gives a choice; they join words or clauses inside one sentence: *I love my country **and** I want to serve it.*

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: Since the local library was renovated last year, the number of visitors ________ significantly.

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The subject is 'the number of visitors' (singular).
The sentence describes an action that started in the past (renovated last year) and continues to have relevance in the present, requiring the present perfect tense ($$\text{has/have} + \text{V}_3$$).
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often see 'visitors' (plural) and choose 'have increased' (Option B).

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The science teacher asked Dawit, 'Why ________ your assignment on time yesterday?'

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
This is a direct question in the past simple tense.
Questions require subject-auxiliary inversion: $$\text{Wh-word} + \text{auxiliary (didn't)} + \text{Subject (you)} + \text{base verb (complete)}$$.
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Option A incorrectly combines 'didn't' with the past tense verb 'completed'.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The rare African manuscript ________ from the national archives before the guards noticed the broken window.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The sentence describes two past events: the manuscript being stolen and the guards noticing the broken window. The theft happened before the guards noticed it, requiring the past perfect passive voice ($$\text{had been} + \text{V}_3$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Option A ('was stolen') is simple past passive. While grammatically correct in isolation, it does not correctly sequence the two past actions. Option D ('has been stolen') is present perfect, which cannot be paired with the simple past past clause ('before the guards noticed').

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እዚ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ክልተ ኣብ ሕሉፍ ግዜ ዝተፈጸሙ ድርጊታት የነጻጽር። እቲ ጽሑፍ ዝተሰረቐሉ ግዜ፡ እቶም ሓለውቲ ቅድሚ ምርኣዮም ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ካብቲ ሓደ ሕሉፍ ግዜ ንላዕሊ ዝቐደመ (earlier past) እዩ። ስለዚ ሕሉፍ ፍጹም ጥንሳዊ መዋቕር (past perfect passive) 'had been stolen' (Option B) ክንጥቀም ኣለና።

The subject of the sentence is 'Each' (singular), which always takes a singular verb and auxiliary ($$\text{Each} \rightarrow \text{singular verb}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often look at the plural noun closest to the verb ('candidates') and incorrectly select the plural auxiliary 'have' (Option B) or 'are' (Option C). This is a classic subject-verb agreement trap.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**

units.title: Politeness
units.intro: Grammar: reported (indirect) speech for statements, questions, requests and commands, and punctuation marks (colon, semi-colon, brackets, hyphen, apostrophe, quotation marks).

cards.title: Reported speech
rule: When the reporting verb is past (*said, asked, told*), the tense usually moves **one step back**: am/is → was; present simple → past simple; past simple → past perfect; will → would; can → could.
Pronouns and time words change: *now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before, here → there*.
**Questions:** *asked + if/whether* (yes/no) or *asked + wh-word*, with **statement word order** and no question mark. **Requests/commands:** *asked/told + object + (not) to + verb*.

examples.text: She said that she was tired.
He asked me where did I live.
examples.fix: He asked me where I lived.

examples.text: The teacher told us to sit down.
She told me don’t go.
examples.fix: She told me not to go.

cards.pattern: said (that) + backshift  ·  asked if/wh- + statement order  ·  told + obj + to-inf

cards.title: Forms and examples
head: Direct
Reported

She asked me to help her.
He told us not to shout.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: One of the most challenging obstacles facing high school graduates ________ the rising cost of higher education.

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The subject of the sentence is 'One' (singular) in the pattern $$\text{One of} + \text{Plural Noun} + \text{Singular Verb}$$.
The plural noun phrase 'the most challenging obstacles' is part of a prepositional phrase modifying the subject.
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often match the verb to the plural noun 'obstacles' which is closest to the verb slot, leading them to choose 'are' (Option A).

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The board of directors, despite having conflicting opinions on the new expansion policy, ________ finally agreed on the budget.

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The subject is 'The board' (singular collective noun).
The phrase 'of directors' and the parenthetical clause 'despite having conflicting opinions...' are intervening elements that do not change the subject's singular number.
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students are often distracted by the plural nouns 'directors' and 'opinions' and select the plural auxiliary 'have' (Option B).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Neither the regional program coordinator nor the senior researchers ________ present at the emergency project meeting yesterday.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The compound subject is connected by the correlative conjunction 'Neither... nor'. The proximity rule applies, meaning the verb agrees with the closer subject, 'the senior researchers' (plural).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students may focus on 'the coordinator' (singular) and choose 'was' (Option A). The past time marker 'yesterday' eliminates present auxiliaries 'is' and 'are', leaving 'were' (Option B) as the correct choice.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ምሉእ ሓሳብ ብ 'Neither... nor' ክእሰር ከሎ፡ እቲ ግሲ ምስቲ ናብኡ ዝቐረበ ባእታ ይሰማማዕ (Proximity Rule)። እቲ ዝቐረበ ባእታ 'the senior researchers' (ብዙሕ) ስለ ዝኾነን እቲ ግዜ ድማ 'yesterday' (ትማሊ) ስለ ዝኾነን፡ ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'were' (Option B) እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The local police ________ currently searching the forest area for the prisoners who escaped from the regional jail.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Police' is a collective noun that is always plural in English and must be paired with plural verbs.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Because 'police' does not end in '-s', students often assume it is singular and choose 'is' (Option A) or 'was' (Option C). The time marker 'currently' indicates present tense, which makes 'are' (Option B) correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Police' (ፖሊስ) ዝብል ስም ብቅርጹ ነጸላ ይመስል እምበር፡ ብሰዋስው ወግዒ ግን ወትሩ ብዙሕ ቁጽሪ (plural) እዩ። 'currently' (ኣብዚ እዋን) ዝብል ቃል ድማ ህልው እዋን ስለ ዝሕብር፡ ምስኡ ዝኸይድ ግሲ 'are' (Option B) እዩ።

units.intro: Grammar: subject–verb agreement (including neither/nor, either/or, together with) and the other parts of speech: adverbs, conjunctions, prepositions and interjections.

cards.title: Subject–verb agreement
rule: A singular subject takes a singular verb (*My friend **lives** here*); a plural subject takes a plural verb (*My friends **live** here*).
With **either ... or** and **neither ... nor**, the verb agrees with the **nearer** subject: *Neither the teacher nor the **students are** here.* / *Either the students or the **teacher is** here.*
**Together with, as well as, along with** do not change the subject: *The captain, together with his players, **is** coming.* **Each, every, everyone, nobody** take a singular verb.

cards.problem: Every morning, my father ________ a cup of traditional coffee before he walks to his office.

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The time-marker 'Every morning' indicates a habitual, repeated action in the present.
This requires the Present Simple tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_{\text{1/s/es}}$$).
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often fail to match the verb to the singular subject 'my father' (3rd person singular), choosing the base form 'drink' (Option C).

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: Listen! The national choir ________ the anthem in the main hall right now.

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The imperative 'Listen!' and 'right now' indicate an action in progress at the exact moment of speaking, requiring the Present Continuous tense ($$\text{S} + \text{am/is/are} + \text{V-ing}$$).
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students must identify 'The national choir' as a singular collective noun, which requires the singular auxiliary 'is'.
Choosing 'are singing' (Option C) is a common agreement error.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Understand' is a stative verb representing a cognitive state. Stative verbs cannot be used in continuous/progressive aspects ($$\times \text{be} + \text{V-ing}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Because Tigrinya often uses continuous structures for states (e.g., 'ይርድኣኒ ኣሎ'), students are highly prone to choosing 'am understanding' (Option A). This is a classic stative verb trap on the ESSLCE.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Understand' (ምርዳእ) ሓደ ካብቶም ናይ ኣእምሮ ኩነታት ዝገልጹ ግሶች (stative verbs) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ቀጻሊ እዋን (progressive aspect) ክወስድ ኣይኽእልን እዩ። ኣብ ትግርኛ 'ይርድኣኒ ኣሎ' (ቀጻሊ ዝመስል) እንተበልና እኳ፡ ብእንግሊዘኛ ግን ወትሩ 'understand' (Option B) ጥራይ ኢና ክንጽሕፍ ዘለና።

cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The conjunction 'While' is followed by the Past Continuous to show a long, ongoing past action. The subject is 'we' (plural), requiring the plural auxiliary 'were'.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students sometimes choose 'waited' (Option A), but 'While' typically requires a continuous tense to establish the background scene ($$\text{while} + \text{was/were} + \text{V-ing}$$).

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'While' (ክነብረና ከለና) ዝብል መስተጻምር ወትሩ ምስ ቀጻሊ ሕሉፍ እዋን (Past Continuous) እዩ ዝኸይድ። እቲ ተግባር (ምጽባይ) ነዊሕ ግዜ ዝወሰደ ኮይኑ፡ ብኻልእ ድንገታዊ ተግባር (ዝናብ ምጅማር) ተቋሪጹ። እቲ ዋና ባእታ 'we' (ብዙሕ) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'were waiting' (Option B) እዩ።

units.intro: Grammar: noun phrases with articles (a/an/the/zero), singular and plural nouns, and tag questions with be, do, have and will.

cards.title: Articles and noun phrases
rule: Use **a** before a consonant sound and **an** before a vowel sound with singular countable nouns mentioned for the first time: *a solar panel, an hour, a university*.
Use **the** when the noun is known or unique: *the sun, the energy we used, the Red Sea*.
Use **no article** (zero) with plural or uncountable nouns in general: *Energy is expensive. Trees give shade.*

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: Aster ________ in this biotechnology laboratory since she graduated from university five years ago.

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**

The time-marker 'since she graduated' indicates an action that started in the past and continues to the present, requiring the Present Perfect Continuous tense ($$\text{S} + \text{has/have been} + \text{V-ing}$$).
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often see 'is working' (Option A) and choose it because they think of it as an ongoing present action.
However, 'since' requires the perfect aspect, making 'has been working' (Option C) correct.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The construction company ________ the new highway road project three weeks ago.

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The definite past time-marker 'three weeks ago' requires the Simple Past tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_2$$).
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often confuse Present Perfect 'has completed' (Option A) with Simple Past 'completed' (Option B).
Present Perfect cannot be used with definite past time-markers like 'three weeks ago'.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Look at those thick dark clouds hanging over the mountains! It ________ rain very soon.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
This is a future prediction based on clear, present physical evidence ('thick dark clouds'). This requires 'be going to' ($$\text{S} + \text{be going to} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often choose 'will' (Option A) for all future predictions. However, when there is clear physical evidence in the present, 'be going to' (Option B) is the grammatically correct choice.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ኣብቲ ከባቢ ንጹር ዝኾነ ናይ ዓይኒ መርትዖ (thick dark clouds - ጸሊም ደበና) ስለ ዘሎ፡ ንመጻኢ ትንቢት ክንገልጽ ከለና 'be going to' (Option B) ክንጥቀም ኣለና። መርትዖ ምስ ዘይህሉ ግን 'will' ምጥቃም ቅኑዕ ምኾነ።

cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The departure of a public train is a formal, timetabled future event that is outside of personal control. This requires the Present Simple tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_{\text{1/s/es}}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often see 'tomorrow' and automatically choose 'will depart' (Option C) or 'is departing' (Option A). However, formal timetables and schedules must be expressed in the Present Simple.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ናይ ባቡር ወይ ነፋሪት መገሻ (timetable) ቀዋሚ ስርዓት ዘለዎ ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ንመጻኢ ግዜ ክንገልጽ ከለና ብ Present Simple 'departs' (Option B) ጥራይ ኢና ክንጽሕፍ ዘለና። 'tomorrow' ስለ ዘሎ 'will depart' ምምራጽ ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Passive in continuous and perfect tenses
rule: **Present continuous passive:** am/is/are + **being** + past participle: *The road **is being repaired**.*
**Past continuous passive:** was/were + **being** + pp: *The hall **was being cleaned** when we arrived.*
**Present perfect passive:** has/have + **been** + pp: *The results **have been published**.* **Past perfect passive:** had + **been** + pp: *The tickets **had been sold** before we came.*

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: I failed the national biology matriculation exam; I ________ harder instead of wasting my time on social media.

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The context 'I failed...; I [blank] harder' indicates a past regret or criticism of an action that was advisable but did not happen.
This requires the past regret modal structure ($$\text{should have} + \text{V}_3$$).
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often confuse 'must have studied' (logical deduction of fact) with 'should have studied' (regret).

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: According to the laboratory safety rules, you ________ enter the chemistry room without wearing safety goggles.

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The context describes a strict laboratory safety rule.
This requires a modal of prohibition to show the action is forbidden ($$\text{must not} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often confuse 'don't have to' (lack of obligation/optional) with 'must not' (prohibition/forbidden).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Aster has been studying and living in London for ten years, so she ________ speak English very fluently.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The context presents strong present evidence ('living in London for ten years'). This requires a modal of present logical deduction to show high certainty ($$\text{must} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students sometimes choose 'must have' (Option D), but 'must have' is for past deduction ($$\text{must have} + \text{V}_3$$) and cannot be followed by the base verb 'speak'. Option A is correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ኣብ ህልው እዋን ዘሎ ናይ ምርግጋጽ ስነ-ሞጎት (present logical deduction) የርእየና። 'ዓሰርተ ዓመት ኣብ ሎንዶን ስለ ዝነበረት' ዝብል መርትዖ ስለ ዘሎ፡ 'ብርግጽ ብጽቡቕ ትዛረብ እያ' ንምባል 'must' (Option A) ክንጥቀም ኣለና። 'must have' ግን ንሕሉፍ እዋን ጥራይ እዩ ዘገልግል።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The soccer field is completely covered in puddles; it ________ heavily during the night.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The present evidence 'The soccer field is completely covered in puddles' leads to a strong positive deduction about a past event. This requires 'must have' ($$\text{must have} + \text{V}_3$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often confuse 'should have rained' (past regret/unrealized advice) with 'must have rained' (past deduction of fact). Option A is incorrect because we are deducing a fact based on physical evidence, making Option B correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'እቲ ናይ ኲዕሶ እግሪ ሜዳ ብማይ ተሸፊኑ ኣሎ' ዝብል ናይ ዓይኒ መርትዖ ስለ ዘለና፡ 'ትማሊ ምሸት ብርግጽ ዓቢ ዝናብ ዘኒቡ ክኸውን ኣለዎ' (past logical deduction) ንምባል 'must have rained' (Option B) ክንመርጽ ኣለና። 'should have' ግን ጣዕሳ ጥራይ እዩ ዝገልጽ።

units.intro: Grammar: talking about the future and conditional sentences type 1 (real/possible) and type 2 (unreal/imaginary).

cards.title: Conditionals type 1 and 2
rule: **Type 1 (real possibility):** *If + present simple, will + base verb.* *If the population **grows** fast, we **will need** more schools.*

**Type 2 (unreal or unlikely now/future):** *If + past simple, would + base verb.* *If I **had** more land, I **would grow** more food.* With be, use **were** for all persons in formal English: *If I **were** you, ...*
The if-clause can come second; then no comma: *We will need more schools if the population grows.*

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: A massive amount of money ________ currently ________ to fund the construction of the new school library.

steps.text: **Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The subject is 'A massive amount of money' (singular and inanimate), requiring the passive voice.
The time-marker 'currently' indicates an action in progress, requiring the Present Progressive Passive ($$\text{is/are} + \text{being} + \text{V}_3$$).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The high school teacher ________ a beautiful traditional gift by the students on her graduation day.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
This is a double-object passive where the Indirect Object 'The high school teacher' is placed in the subject position: $$\text{IO} + \text{be} + \text{V}_3 + \text{DO}$$.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often choose 'gave' (Option A) because they see a person as the subject and assume the active voice. However, the context shows she received the gift, requiring the passive form 'was given' (Option B).

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ መምህር ባዕሉ ህያብ ኣይሃበን፤ বልኩስ ካብ ተመሃሮ ህያብ ተዋሂብዎ (received)። እዚ ዓይነት መዋቕር ድርብ ተቐባሊ ዘለዎ ግሲ (double-object passive) ኮይኑ፡ 'was given' (Option B - ተዋሂቡ) ቅኑዕ መልሲ ይኸውን። 'gave' እንተይልና እቲ መምህር ባዕሉ ንተመሃሮ ህያብ ሂብዎም ማለት ምኾነ።

cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The inanimate subject 'examination papers' requires the passive voice. The time-marker 'by next Friday' indicates a future point of completion, requiring the Future Perfect Passive ($$\text{will have been} + \text{V}_3$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often see 'next Friday' and choose active 'will print' (Option A) or active future perfect 'will have printed' (Option D). Because papers cannot print themselves, the passive 'will have been printed' (Option B) is correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'By next Friday' (ክሳብ ዝመጽእ ዓርቢ) ዝብል ሓረግ መጻኢ ፍጹም እዋን (Future Perfect) ከም ዘድልየና የረድኣና። እቲ ዋና ባእታ 'examination papers' (መፈተኒ ወረቐት) ህይወት ኣልቦ ስለ ዝኾነ ድማ እቲ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ኣብ Future Perfect Passive 'will have been printed' (Option B - ተሓቲሙ ክውዳእ እዩ) ክስራዕ ኣለዎ።
